messages:
From: Emma Collins <emma.collins@brightedge.com>

Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick question on reference timing & substitutes

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the product demo last week. We're lining up customer advocates for an exec-level validation call and I wanted to confirm a couple of operational details on your side so we can schedule with minimal friction:

- Do you maintain a blackout/opt-out window where advocates should not be scheduled (e.g., QBRs, end-of-quarter busy periods)?
- If an advocate needs to decline at short notice, what's the substitute process and typical lead time?
- Any limits on how many times a single advocate can be asked in a quarter?

If you have a short doc you can share outlining the rules, that would be great — saves us from back-and-forth. We want to be mindful of advocate fatigue.

Best,
Emma Collins
Product Ops
BrightEdge

P.S. Proposed dates for the exec call: 2026-07-20 or 2026-07-22 (PST).

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-09T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on reference timing & substitutes

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the clear list — this is exactly the sort of question we want to avoid surprises on. Attached is our short internal guide and the current advocate roster (redacted contact info where requested). High level answers below, and Rafael (cc) can jump in if you'd like official stance or account-level exceptions.

- Blackout/opt-out windows: We ask customers to provide any blackout windows at least 14 days ahead of proposed dates. For advocates themselves, we enforce an internal 10-business-day notice for scheduling whenever possible to avoid last-minute conflicts.
- Substitute process: If an advocate declines within the 10-business-day window, we aim to provide a substitute within 48 hours. If decline occurs inside 48 hours of the event, we escalate to the account lead for possible reschedule or identify an alternate advocate from a secondary pool.
- Frequency limit: Our default policy is no more than 2 customer-facing reference asks per advocate per quarter. Exceptions (e.g., reference-led case studies) can be approved by the account manager.

Attachment: BrightEdge_advocate_optout_policy.docx (policy summary)
Attachment: advocate_pool_v2.csv (advocate list with opt-out flags)

If those timelines create conflicts with your proposed dates (7/20 and 7/22), let me know and we can either prioritize one date and push the other or confirm an alternate advocate.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Emma —

Two quick clarifications from an operations standpoint:

- Lead time: We prefer a 10-business-day lead for primary advocates and a 5-business-day lead for substitutes. That lets us avoid asking people during internal busy windows (quarter ends, product launches).
- Substitute roster: We keep a small "hot" roster of advocates who have opted in for short-notice asks (they get an extra thank-you credit). If a substitute from that pool accepts within 24–48 hours, we won't count it against the standard frequency limit.
- Decline logging: Please reply-all when a decline happens so we can record it in the advocate tracker — we audit requests monthly to monitor fatigue.

Also, please confirm whether BrightEdge needs NDA redaction or if this is just a short reference call. If you anticipate a recorded case study, we'll need the extra contract step (legal review).

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Advocacy | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Emma —

Appreciate the heads-up and for moving to 7/22. Couple of operational notes — copying Kar thik (advocate ops) since he manages substitutions and incentive credits: 

- Scheduling workflow: For substitutes we prefer the account team (Marissa) coordinate outreach to avoid duplicate invites; however, if you want Jorge to manage availability checks, that's fine as long as Marissa stays in the loop and confirms the final pick.
- Short-notice substitute credits: We offer a modest thank-you credit ($150 equivalent vendor gift card or a donation in their name) for substitutes who accept within 72 hours. This reserve is approved at the regional sales ops level for US accounts. Kar thik will process the credit once the substitute confirms.
- Tracking & decline logging: Please include the decline reason in the reply-all (we log 'decline reason' so we can analyze patterns). If declines become frequent for a given advocate we will rotate them to the secondary list.
- Escalation: If a substitute cannot be found within 24 hours of the event, we can either reschedule or offer a product SME instead (typically more technical, shorter duration).

I'll have Kar thik reach out to Jorge directly to get availability and confirm the final advocate no later than 7/19 EOD. If you'd like a formal one-page SOW addendum for the reference call (recording permissions, NDAs, etc.), Marissa can route that to Legal.

Thanks —
